verses.text: Moses answered, "But what if they do not believe me or listen to me? What if they say, 'The LORD did not appear to you'?"
The LORD asked him, "What is that in your hand?" "A staff," Moses answered.
The LORD said, "Throw it on the ground." So Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake. Moses ran away from it.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Reach out your hand and take it by the tail." So Moses reached out and caught it, and it turned back into a staff in his hand.
"Do this," the LORD said, "so that they will believe that the LORD, the God of their ancestors, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you."
Then the LORD said, "Put your hand inside your coat." So Moses put his hand inside his coat. When he took it out, his hand had a skin disease. It was as white as snow.
"Now put your hand back inside your coat," God said. So Moses put his hand back inside his coat. When he took it out, it was healthy again, like the rest of his body.
Then the LORD said, "If they do not believe you or pay attention to the first sign, they may believe the second sign.

And if they do not believe even these two signs or listen to you, take some water from the River Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water you take from the river will turn into blood on the ground."
Moses said to the LORD, "Please, Lord, I have never been good with words, not in the past, and not since you started speaking to me, your servant. I speak slowly, and my tongue is slow."
The LORD said to him, "Who gave people their mouths? Who makes them unable to speak or hear? Who makes them able to see, or makes them blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
So go now. I will help you speak, and I will teach you what to say."
But Moses said, "Please, Lord, send someone else."
Then the LORD became angry with Moses. He said, "What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he can speak well. He is already on his way to meet you, and he will be glad when he sees you.
You will speak to him and tell him what to say. I will help both of you speak, and I will teach you what to do.
He will speak to the people for you. He will be like your mouth, and you will be like God to him.
And take this staff in your hand, so that you can do the signs with it."

Then Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, "Please let me go back to my own people in Egypt to see if any of them are still alive." Jethro said to Moses, "Go, and peace be with you."
The LORD had said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, because all the men who wanted to kill you are dead."
So Moses put his wife and sons on a donkey and started back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.

The LORD said to Moses, "When you get back to Egypt, make sure you do in front of Pharaoh all the wonders I have given you the power to do. But I will make him stubborn, so that he will not let the people go.
Then say to Pharaoh, 'This is what the LORD says: Israel is my son, my firstborn son.
I told you, "Let my son go, so that he can worship me." But you refused to let him go. So now I will kill your firstborn son.'"
On the way, at a place where they stopped for the night, the LORD met Moses and was about to kill him.
But Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off her son's foreskin, and touched Moses' feet with it. Then she said, "You are a husband of blood to me."
So the LORD left him alone. At that time she said "husband of blood" because of the circumcision.
The LORD said to Aaron, "Go into the desert to meet Moses." So Aaron went and met Moses at the mountain of God, and he kissed him.
Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and about all the signs the LORD had commanded him to do.
Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the leaders of the people of Israel.
Aaron told them everything the LORD had said to Moses. He also did the signs in front of the people,
and the people believed. When they heard that the LORD had come to help the people of Israel and had seen their suffering, they bowed down and worshipped.
